The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, or RSS, the "national volunteer organisation", was founded at Nagpur on 27 September 1925 by K. B. Hedgewar, a doctor. It is the parent body of Hindu nationalism in India and one of the largest voluntary organisations in the world.

Its idea is Hindutva, set out by V. D. Savarkar in 1923: India is the homeland and holy land of the Hindus, and the nation should be built on Hindu culture. Critics say this makes Muslims and Christians second-class citizens.

The RSS works through the shakha, a daily hour of drill, games, songs and talks for boys and men in uniform, held in a park or yard. It has tens of thousands of these. Full-time organisers, who do not marry, run it. It kept out of the Quit India Movement and of electoral politics.

It has been banned three times. The first was in 1948, after a former member shot Gandhi (see the assassination). The others were during the Emergency and after the Babri Masjid was pulled down in 1992.

Around it grew a family of linked bodies: trade unions, schools, student groups and a party, since 1980 the Bharatiya Janata Party. The prime ministers Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Narendra Modi both began as RSS organisers.
